doc_summary: the open screen hears of a key press (`native_screen_key_pressed_pre`) and of each character it types (`native_screen_char_typed_pre`), as vanilla's `ScreenEvent.KeyPressed.Pre` and `.CharacterTyped.Pre`: the screen, vanilla's key name (`key.keyboard.e`, as `native_key` hands it over; a key with no name fires nothing), whether the press is an auto-repeat, the character, GLFW's modifier bits (shift 1, control 2, alt 4, super 8), and `screen.mouse` for the pointer. A cancelled press goes no further — no focus move, no Escape-close, no inventory or hotbar key, no typing by the key itself, no `native_key` — while its release still arrives, so a `native_key` listener sees that release without its press, and the characters no mod cancelled still reach the text box, as vanilla's separate `charTyped` comes for a cancelled `keyPressed` too. A cancelled character drops only that character and never reaches a text box; control characters (Enter, Backspace, Tab, Delete, Escape, a Control letter) are keys and fire nothing. A key's characters fire after the key has acted, as GLFW's char callback comes after its key callback, so a key that closes the screen (the inventory key) reports no character (the closed screen hears none) and one that moves the focus types into the box it moved to. The input method's committed text fires the character hook too. They fire for the window and the control socket's `key` and `type` (not its `\b` backspace), after the fullscreen, screenshot, debug and narrator keys, never on the title screen itself (Options and the pack list opened from it do fire), the connect and loading screens, the prompts, books and sign editors drawn over gameplay, or while a world loads or saves. Bundles need "hooks": @API:screen_key_input@.
